chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who causes another man to startle, so he wounds him, and his riding animal wounds another man. He said: “He is liable for whatever resulted from that.” And what further clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.فَيَعْقِرُهُ: so he wounds or injures him

ai.seo_question: Is a person legally liable if frightening someone causes injuries to others?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on liability for harm caused by frightening or provoking a person in a way that leads to injury. It establishes that the one who initiated the cause is responsible for the resulting damage, including consequential harm involving the injured person’s animal.
